purpose: Audit why D272 boundary-only final-selection gain disappears when the boundary score is constrained to preserve D262 validation behavior.

tradeoff.alpha_grid_note: Final labels are not used to choose policy; this grid is diagnostic only and shows why the boundary-only rescue needs much more weight than validation-preserving policies.

findings: The selected hybrid alpha 0.3 is below the minimum alpha 2.306844 needed to recover the lost boundary-only final rescue.
At alpha 2.5, diagnostic final selection reaches 5/8 while existing validation is 18/24.
The boundary-only rescue is not a small calibration effect; it requires overriding a large D262 margin on a final diagnostic example.

decision.reason: Recovering the lost boundary-only rescue requires alpha about 2.306844 versus selected alpha 0.3, so this is not a safe small-weight hybrid.
decision.next_step: Keep D262 as active baseline and audit the lost-rescue example as a possible answer-generation/ranking margin problem rather than buying more broad labels.

llm_budget.note: This audit reads existing selector artifacts only.
